## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `--exclude` flag needs an `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` environment default, because the project's CLI flag rules require one for every flag added under `cli/`. This review found no other defect in the exclusion logic, its tests, or the docs row.

## Changes
The pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag to `cli/main.py` that makes `collect()` skip files whose base name matches any pattern, and logs each skipped path. It also adds a row to `docs/flags.md`, five tests in `tests/test_main.py`, and a fixture file `tests/fixtures/hostile-review.txt`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Take the `--exclude` default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` — Running with `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE=*.log` set and no `--exclude` still archives `.log` files, because the flag hard-codes `default=[]`. `.claude/skills/cli-flags/reference.md:5` requires: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". — CI, which sets options through the environment, cannot configure exclusions, so files it means to skip end up in the archive. — Fix: Read the default from `os.environ.get("ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE")`, choose and document a separator for multiple globs in `docs/flags.md`, and extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing` to cover the variable.
